images.filename: A rubberized squid- yes, that was a live squid once! (20564597380).jpg
images.caption: From rubber dinosaur models to rubberized real creatures. Yes, that was once a live squid swimming in the seas near you. After death, silicone was injected into the creature's body to rubberize it and to preserve all it's natural muscles and fibres. This concept was tried with human bodies initially, where an exhibition in China caused much uproar in 1995. People soon got over it, and rubberized real human exhibits are quite common nowadays. Mercifully we didn't see any rubberized human bodies, barring a human heart and a brain (we were encouraged to hold the heart in our hand!), but in this section we saw several siliconized animals. More notes in subsequent captions. (Ottawa, Canada, June 2015)

images.filename: A real ostrich, rubberized after death (20128495004).jpg
images.caption: The real squid rubberized and preserved had fascinated me enough, but I was hardly prepared for this! At least with the squid, one couldn't see the muscles and flesh tissues. Hhere in this rubberized Ostrich, it's all there for you to see. Yes, that was once a real, living ostrich. Injecting silicone inside it has preserved all it's muscles and tissues. Bright spotlighting has over exposed the picture somewhet, sorry about that. Notes about rubberizing animal bodies appear in previous captions. (Ottawa, Canada, June 2015)

images.filename: City buses to the Quebec side are blue- white (20564125760).jpg
images.caption: While the ubiquitous red- white city buses on Ottawa's British (Ontario) buses are run by OC Transpo, on the French (Quebec) side, the city bus operator is Société de Transport de l’Outaouais. Here instead of red- white, the buses are characterised by turquoise- white livery. Here is one of the buses from the Quebec on a routine run on Queen's St. Although these are two separate operators, buses cross freely from the Ontario to the Quebec side and vice versa, though inside their territories, local services are run by their own operator. (Ottawa, Canada, June 2015)
